patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Jira and Wrike share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Frame: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Jira and Wrike share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.. Choose Jira only if your buying job matches “Atlassian Agile issue tracker for software teams — Free ≤10; Standard from ~$8.15/user/mo ” rather than Wrike's shape. Choose Wrike only if your buying job matches “Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team from $10/use” rather than Jira's shape. Workflow advantage: Jira leans shared coverage; Wrike leans resource-planning, team-collaboration-work. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Jira and Wrike share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Jira is Atlassian Agile issue tracker for software teams — Free ≤10; Standard from ~$8.15/user/mo annual.; Wrike is Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team from $10/user/mo annual..
- Workflow coverage skew: Jira-leaning — vs Wrike-leaning resource-planning, team-collaboration-work.
- Researched limits: Jira — Steep learning curve outside engineering; Wrike — Business tier pricing jump.

Limitations — Jira: Steep learning curve outside engineering; Confluence often required for wiki/docs depth; Wrike: Business tier pricing jump; Heavier admin than lightweight tools.

Poor-fit cases: Jira is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Steep learning curve outside engineering · Wrike is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Business tier pricing jump · Avoid Jira if you actually need Wrike's motion (Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team fr)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
